headline: Copper Moves Lower as US Election Undermines AI and Tariff Trade
author: Bloomberg News

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:26 PM CST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Copper slumped to its lowest since July as a political shakeup in Washington threatened to blunt two key bullish drivers: the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure, and the risk of US import tariffs on the metal.

Industrial metals have joined a broader flight from risk since the Democrats swept Congress, as technology stocks tumble on concerns over tighter regulation on artificial intelligence. Copper, used in cables and wiring for data centers and power equipment, fell as much as 0.8%, after a 1.2% decline on Thursday.

The Republican wipeout — fueled by angst over inflation — has also triggered fresh speculation about the chances of expanded US import tariffs on copper. The prospect of fees had kept US prices higher and tightened the global market by pulling in huge volumes to American stockpiles. On Thursday, that price differential disappeared.

"Many traders believe aggressive copper tariffs are now less likely with the Democratic Party controlling the US Congress, with affordability being the Achilles heel for the governing party heading into 2028," TD Securities said in a note.
Copper dipped 0.4% to $13,786 a ton on the London Metal Exchange as of 9:23 a.m. in Shanghai. Aluminum and zinc fell 0.5%.
